_readme: Inheritance-only bloodline slots (Saga) for traits spec §3.5a at commit 0bd80b1. Six of the approved 56 traits are blood-only: giant, long_sabers, frost_hardy, fertile, long_lived, tainted_blood. For each trait, one premade shows it and two carry it, except tainted_blood (nobody shows, two carry, a hidden family flaw). No cat shows more than one inherit-only trait. Slot ids are used because names roll each run (world-gen §3). Shows sit on current pride members so the bloodline is visible in a pride; loners are used as carriers, and as the two tainted_blood carriers. Family links are used only where the docs state them. A second carrier is sometimes in another pride with no claimed kinship, so the trait is not bottled in one roster. Rumours reuse traits-copy-v1.json (two told lines per trait) and are refined to pass-2 style. {name} and {subjectName} bind to the same subject cat. Do not edit or commit this into the sabretooth repo; it is Saga working copy.

_source.existingTraitSheet: No Saga 0-2 mechanical trait sheet was in the repo or on origin/cursor/recurring-conversation-proof-ddae or b9aacb4. loners.json 'traits' are narrative lean words, not the 56-trait ids. Portrait defaults have no size or trait flags.

_tokens.name: The cat the rumour is about. Same binding as lore-book {subjectName}.
_tokens.subjectName: Lore Book subject token. Bind to the same cat as {name}, as traits-copy-v1.json notes.
_tokens.sourceName: The cat who passed the rumour on.

_rules.carriersHidden: A carrier gets no effect and is not shown as having the trait. The Lore Book only knows carriers as rumours (§3.4a, §3.5a.2).
_rules.taintedBloodRumours: Vague family talk. Never name the carriers as fact, and never use their slot ids or role names in the told lines.
_rules.founder: Not assigned here. The player's founder rolls spontaneous 1% to show each trait and a hidden 10% to carry each (§3.5a.6).

why.bf01: Scarjaw is the only premade the lore calls a heavy tom, and he holds Bonefield by challenge, so he can show Giant.
why.bf08: Scarjaw and bf04's adolescent daughter, so the line can pass or skip in the next generation.
why.mw03: Young Mistwood tom with no size lore, so a hidden carry is safe and moves the bloodline out of Bonefield. No documented kin link.

why.hc03: Ashmane's mate and Highcrag's big-game hunter, with throat-bite training; long sabers fit a pride that recites its bloodlines.
why.hc02: Stonebrow, their son, so the blood can pass without a second show.
why.bf03: Bonefield hunter with the same big-game skills and no saber-injury lore. No documented kin link; used to spread the trait.

why.hc08: Highcrag's recitation keeper, lives on the wind-scoured crag, and already holds thickCoat with winter_coat.
why.ln01: Greymantle ranges the Ice Wall and has the vale's highest thick-coat training. A loner, so he carries rather than shows.
why.mw02: Older Mistwood tom with thickCoat, snow_sleeper and den_maker, and he survived the Breaking. No documented kin to hc08.

why.hc06: Highcrag nursemaid who already has two cubs and is still young, well inside the fertile window.
why.hc10: Her older cub, so the line can stay hidden and show later.
why.bf04: Scarjaw's mate, also has two cubs and is still breeding age. No documented kin to hc06; used to spread the trait.

why.mw07: Oldest cat in the vale, Mistwood's wise-cat, with hardiness at its cap and the long_life perk.
why.ln06: Lichen has the same long_life perk, but lore calls her too frail to cross the marsh, so she only carries.
why.bf07: Tallgrass's old guard, still on duty after Scarjaw's rise. No documented kin to mw07; used to spread the trait.

why.ln03: Torncheek, half-brother of Duskrunner through the hidden Bonefield sire off_bf_sire. Not described as sickly, which fits a hidden carry.
why.ln05: Duskrunner, the other living cub of that hidden sire. The flaw stays in one family, and nobody shows it.

giant.text: {sourceName} says {name} stands a head above any cat in the Vale. Hard to say if that's true.
They say {name} is huge, though {sourceName} only saw it from across the river.

long_sabers.text: {sourceName} says {name}'s sabers hang nearly to the chest. That's the story, anyway.
They say {name} has the longest sabers in the Vale. {sourceName} might be stretching it.

frost_hardy.text: {sourceName} says {name} sleeps out in blizzards and wakes up fine. That's what they say.
By {sourceName}'s telling, {name} walked through a whiteout like it was summer.

fertile.text: {sourceName} says {name} comes from a line with big litters. Hard to know for sure.
They say {name}'s blood is strong for cubs. {sourceName} heard it from an old cat.

long_lived.text: {sourceName} says {name}'s line stays strong long after others go grey.
By {sourceName}'s telling, {name} will see more winters than most.

tainted_blood.text: Quietly, {sourceName} says sickness runs in {name}'s line. That's the talk.
Word is the cubs in {name}'s family come weak. {sourceName} wouldn't say where that talk started.
tainted_blood.refinedFrom: traits-copy-v1.json (vaguer family talk, no claim that the subject is a carrier)
